summary: H1 (confidence 0.86, high) is the root cause: the cfg-3120 flag ramp on pricing-engine (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5 → 100 at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z) put all pricing-engine traffic onto the CPU-bound Greeks v2 Monte-Carlo path, saturating CPU and inflating p99 from ~59ms to ~2.6s while request rate stayed flat — which broke order-service's 2500ms client timeout on its direct pricing-engine quote call. The mechanism is directly witnessed in pricing-engine's own logs (flag applied 12:04:16Z, then "GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms" from 12:05:21Z and "request deadline exceeded ... calculator=GreeksV2" errors), and the ordering/scope/signature all line up: pricing-engine's CPU, p99 and 5xx jump together in the 12:04 bucket before order-service degrades in the 12:06 bucket, with every order-service error carrying the single downstream signature "pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms". The competing capacity/saturation recurrence (H2) is contradicted by flat RPS at constant load plus zero restarts and zero scaling events, and the shared redis-cache origin (H3) is contradicted by flat hit ratio, evictions and client count across the onset with no cache WARN+ logs. The reporter's market-data-service protobuf deploy suspicion is cleanly rejected: its p99 stayed flat at ~35-44ms throughout, there is an 8-minute quiet gap after that deploy, and no serialization-change precedent exists.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine Greeks v2 feature-flag ramp to 100% causes CPU saturation and quote timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 12:04:00Z the config change cfg-3120 (flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5 → 100) ramped the Greeks v2 Monte-Carlo computation to all pricing-engine traffic. That code path is CPU-bound and expensive (per-request Monte-Carlo with paths=20000), driving pricing-engine cpu_pct from ~40% to ~98-100% and p99 from ~59ms to ~2.6s in the same 12:04 bucket — at CONSTANT request rate (~606-687 req/s, no step). order-service's quote path calls pricing-engine directly (F9), so its quote calls exceeded the 2500ms client timeout, producing the observed 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' errors.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-3120 ramps flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5 → 100 at 12:04:00Z on pricing-engine

The Greeks v2 code path is executed for all traffic and pricing-engine logs show the flag applied at 12:04:16Z, with GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo slowness immediately after (first WARN 12:05:21Z 'paths=20000 took 6465ms'; 44 WARNs + 32 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' ERRORs)

pricing-engine CPU rises at constant load: RPS FLAT at ~606-687 req/s across 11:50-12:20Z with no step at 12:04Z (F19), while cpu_pct goes ~39-41% flat through 12:02Z → avg 68.44/max 98.65 in the 12:04 bucket → pinned ~98.7-99.6% from 12:06Z (F20). CPU rose at constant RPS.
pricing-engine p99 jumps from ~59ms to avg 1297.72 / max 2534.9ms in the same 12:04 bucket, reaching ~2.6-2.7s thereafter
pricing-engine itself returns ~12% 5xx server-side (0.2% → 9.75% avg in the 12:04 bucket, holding ~12.3-12.75%)
pricing-engine degrades in the 12:04 bucket, before order-service degrades in the 12:06 bucket
order-service quote calls to pricing-engine exceed the 2500ms client timeout, yielding 225 ERROR entries with signature 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' from 12:06:10Z onward

assumptions: No other change in the partial config-audit shard 2/3 contributed (shard 2/3 never independently confirmed)

Greeks v2's specific CPU cost is inferred from its own 6465ms Monte-Carlo WARN logs rather than from a CPU profile

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine CPU saturation from load outgrowing provisioned capacity (recurrence of HIST-113)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine's CPU saturation and 2.6s p99 are driven by request volume outgrowing provisioned capacity at a market-open-style traffic peak, not by any faulty change. Consistent with HIST-113 ('Record market-open volume exceeded provisioned capacity', quote timeouts + cpu 99%, resolved by raising replica count), order-service timeouts are the downstream consequence of a saturated pricing-engine that cannot absorb the load.

causal_chain.claim: pricing-engine request volume/load exceeds provisioned capacity around 12:04Z
pricing-engine CPU pins at ~98-100% from the 12:04 bucket onward
pricing-engine p99 rises from ~59ms to ~2.6s and error_rate to ~12%
Downstream order-service quote calls time out at 2500ms, producing the observed ERROR signature

assumptions: Load on pricing-engine rose independently of the 12:04 config ramp (contradicted: RPS is flat)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared redis-cache degradation starves pricing-engine (dependency/infrastructure failure on a shared datastore)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The platform-owned, shared=true redis-cache sits on pricing-engine's quote path. A redis-cache degradation or cold-cache/contention event (as in HIST-107, 'Cold cache storm after redis failover') would make pricing-engine block on cache I/O, producing CPU-busy latency inflation, elevated 5xx, and downstream order-service timeouts. Under this hypothesis the fault originates in shared infrastructure, not in pricing-engine's own code or config.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache (platform-owned, shared=true) is on the pricing-engine quote path

redis-cache degrades (failover/eviction/cold-cache storm or contention) around 12:04Z — NOT observed: all three queried facets are flat through onset (hit ratio ~97% F25, evictions ~3/min F26, connected_clients ~300-335 F27), and zero WARN+ redis-cache logs in 08:00-13:59Z (F28)
pricing-engine blocks on cache calls, inflating CPU-busy latency to ~2.6s p99 and error_rate to ~12%
order-service quote calls to pricing-engine exceed 2500ms and time out

assumptions: redis-cache latency/error/failover cannot be measured from its exposed metrics (F29), so the 'healthy cache' conclusion rests on hit ratio, evictions and client count only

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy (dep-6111) degrades its callers, cascading to order-service (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: market-data-service dep-6111 v5.2.0 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' at 11:56:00Z introduced a slow/blocking encode path. Because pricing-engine calls market-data-service (F9/F16), the slow encode path stalls pricing-engine's quote handler, which in turn makes order-service quote calls time out.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6111 v5.2.0 switches market-data-service quote serialization to protobuf at 11:56:00Z and is not rolled back
The protobuf encode path is slow/blocking for the quote payloads market-data-service serves
market-data-service latency rises at onset
pricing-engine, which calls market-data-service, blocks on those calls and its p99 rises to ~2.6s
order-service quote calls to pricing-engine exceed 2500ms and time out

assumptions: An encode-path regression would show up in market-data-service's own p99 (contradicted: flat ~35-44ms)
The 8-minute gap between the 11:56 deploy and the 12:04 onset reflects delayed activation rather than irrelevance
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service p99 stayed flat at ~35-44ms across the entire 11:00-13:59Z window including the onset buckets (F4), so it is not in the latency blast radius; there is an 8-minute quiet gap between the 11:56 deploy and the 12:04 pricing-engine jump (F2/F7); no historical precedent exists for a market-data-service serialization change causing timeouts (F14); and pricing-engine's own logs directly attribute the slowness to GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo, not to a downstream call (F24). One caveat: market-data-service error_rate/CPU were never queried, so this rejection rests mainly on the p99 evidence.

ranked_hypotheses.statement: An order-service-local change or resource exhaustion (thread pool, db connection pool to shared ledger-db, or timeout configuration) shortly before onset causes quote-request timeouts regardless of downstream latency; the market-data-service correlation is spurious.

findings.statement: Second precedent lead HIST-107 (2025-12-09, 'Cold cache storm after redis failover') affected services redis-cache and market-data-service with symptom 'quote latency', root cause 'Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica', resolved by warming the cache and fixing replica sync checks. This is relevant because the shared, platform-owned redis-cache sits on the quote path: the current dependency graph shows edges pricing-engine→redis-cache (cache) and market-data-service→redis-cache (cache).

refs.quote: Cold cache storm after redis failover
Redis primary failure promoted an empty replica

findings.statement: Dependency mapping of the current quote path confirms: pricing-engine (owner 'trading', shared=false) calls market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache); market-data-service in turn calls redis-cache and exchange-gateway (http). order-service calls pricing-engine (http), and api-gateway calls order-service. market-data-service and redis-cache are the only shared nodes (market-data-service shared=false per node list; redis-cache shared=true), so pricing-engine's own saturation cannot be attributed to a shared datastore contention unless redis-cache itself is degraded.

findings.statement: A config/flag-change precedent pattern exists alongside the deployment-rollback pattern: HIST-115 (2025-09-25, 'order-service connection pool misconfiguration') has symptoms 'connection is not available','request timed out','pool exhausted', root cause 'Datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile', category config_change, resolution 'Reverted config; added validation'. This shows config/flag reverts (not just code deploys) are an established mitigation for timeout incidents on this platform.

findings.statement: Comparing the current change list (T2/F7/F8) against precedent causes: the current window's only deployment (market-data-service dep-6111 v5.2.0 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' at 11:56:00Z, not rolled back) and only config change (pricing-engine cfg-3120 flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5→100 at 12:04:00Z) do NOT correspond to any historical incident titled around serialization, whereas the pricing-engine CPU 99% + quote-timeout symptom set matches HIST-113 exactly. This is an inference drawn from precedent leads, not proof of the current cause.

findings.statement: pricing-engine request_rate was FLAT across the whole 11:50-12:20Z window: values oscillate ~606-687 req/s with no step at 12:04Z (11:58=606.28, 12:00=647.2, 12:02=667.24, 12:04=625.14, 12:06=666.82, 12:08=646.04, 12:10=616.42). Summary min 590.66 / max 687.48 / mean 642.59. Throughput did not increase at the flag ramp.

pricing-engine cpu_pct at the same 2-min resolution was ~39-41% flat through 12:02Z, then in the 12:04 bucket avg 68.44 / max 98.65 (ramping mid-bucket) and pinned at ~98.7-99.6% from 12:06Z onward (12:06=98.67, 12:08=99.34, max 100.0). The CPU ramp coincides with the 12:04Z flag change while RPS is unchanged -> CPU rose at constant load.

pricing-engine exposes no replica_count and no queue_depth/in-flight metric — the only available metrics are cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts. So a direct replica-count or autoscaling event could NOT be measured from metrics.

pricing-engine restarts (cumulative) stayed exactly 0.0 for every 2-min bucket from 11:50Z through 12:20Z (min 0.0, max 0.0, missing_points 0), i.e. no pod restart/replacement occurred during onset, and memory_pct stayed flat ~48-51% throughout — memory pressure is not the saturation driver.

No autoscaling-scale log lines exist for pricing-engine in 11:45-12:20Z (contains='scal' returned 0 matches vs a data range 08:00-13:59Z), so there is no evidence of any scale-up/scale-down event in the window.

pricing-engine's own logs show the flag applied at 12:04:16Z and GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo slowness beginning immediately after: first WARN at 12:05:21Z 'GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms', 44 such WARNs plus 32 ERRORs 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' (first error 12:06:41Z). First match 12:04:16Z, last 12:19:59Z (truncated=true, 30 of 77 returned).

refs.quote: GreeksV2Calculator: Monte-Carlo paths=20000 took 6465ms for symbol opt-41547

findings.statement: redis-cache hit ratio is flat through the onset: baseline 11:50-12:02 averages ~94.7-97.2%, and the onset buckets are 12:04 avg 97.11 / max 98.46 and 12:06 avg 96.44, i.e. no cache-miss storm or drop in hit rate at 12:02-12:06Z (window min 93.83, max 98.46, mean 96.19).

redis-cache evictions_per_min show no eviction storm at onset: the series stays in a narrow ~2-4 keys/min band across 11:50-12:20Z (12:04 avg 2.75/max 3.35, 12:06 avg 3.75/max 3.76; window min 2.15, max 4.31, mean 3.15), with no jump at 12:02-12:06Z.

redis-cache connected_clients is flat through the onset with no connection spike or collapse: 314-336 clients around 12:00-12:02 (12:00 avg 324.72, 12:02 avg 326.45), 306.24 at 12:04 and 297.69 at 12:06; window range 288.17-335.37, mean 311.86.

There are ZERO redis-cache log entries at WARN or above for the whole 08:00-13:59Z data range (total_matched 0, returned 0, not truncated), so no redis-cache failover/restart/error event was logged in the incident window or the hours before it.

redis-cache exposes no latency, connection-error, or failover/restart metric at all: available_metrics = [connected_clients, cpu_pct, evictions_per_min, hit_ratio_pct, memory_pct], and a latency_p99_ms query was rejected with 'service redis-cache has no metric latency_p99_ms'. So the instrumented facets of redis-cache are consistent with a healthy cache, but latency/error/failover cannot be measured from metrics for this component.

Across the three queried redis-cache facets (hit ratio, evictions, client count) there is no metric step at the 12:02-12:06Z onset that matches the pricing-engine latency/CPU step at 12:04Z; redis-cache is flat across the step, which is a distinctly different signature from the CPU-saturation and 5xx step seen on pricing-engine.
